questions.question: Explain how React's virtual DOM and reconciliation work. Why does this improve performance?

rubric.point: Virtual DOM is an in-memory representation of the UI
Diffing compares the new tree with the previous one
Only the changed nodes are updated in the real DOM
Keys help identify list items during reconciliation

questions.question: What is the difference between useEffect and useLayoutEffect? Give a use case for each.

rubric.point: useEffect runs after paint, asynchronously
useLayoutEffect runs synchronously before the browser paints
useLayoutEffect is for DOM measurements / avoiding flicker
useEffect for data fetching or subscriptions

questions.question: How would you improve the performance of a slow React page that renders a list of 10,000 rows?

rubric.point: Virtualization / windowing of the list
Memoization with React.memo / useMemo / useCallback
Stable keys to avoid unnecessary re-renders
Pagination or lazy loading

questions.question: Explain the CSS box model and the difference between box-sizing: content-box and border-box.

rubric.point: Box model = content, padding, border, margin
content-box width excludes padding and border
border-box width includes padding and border

questions.question: How do you manage global state in a React application? Compare Context API with Redux.

rubric.point: Context API shares state without prop drilling
Redux uses a single store, actions and reducers
Context can cause re-renders of all consumers
Redux has devtools / middleware, better for large apps

questions.question: What are the benefits of TypeScript in a frontend codebase? Mention at least three.

rubric.point: Static type checking catches errors at compile time
Better IDE autocomplete / refactoring
Self-documenting interfaces and props

questions.question: Explain how Spring Boot auto-configuration works.

rubric.point: @SpringBootApplication / @EnableAutoConfiguration triggers it
Configuration classes are conditionally applied based on the classpath
Starters bring in dependencies and defaults
Defaults can be overridden with properties or custom beans

questions.question: What is the difference between @Transactional propagation REQUIRED and REQUIRES_NEW?

rubric.point: REQUIRED joins an existing transaction or creates one
REQUIRES_NEW always starts a new transaction
REQUIRES_NEW suspends the outer transaction
Use case: audit logging that must commit independently

questions.question: How would you design a REST API for transferring money between two accounts safely?

rubric.point: POST endpoint with idempotency key
Database transaction / atomic debit and credit
Locking or optimistic concurrency to avoid double spend
Validation, proper HTTP status codes and audit trail

questions.question: Explain the N+1 query problem in JPA/Hibernate and how to fix it.

rubric.point: One query for parent then one per child (lazy loading)
Fix with JOIN FETCH or entity graphs
Batch fetching / @BatchSize

questions.question: What are the pros and cons of microservices compared to a monolith?

rubric.point: Independent deployment and scaling
Technology and team autonomy
Operational complexity: network, monitoring, distributed tracing
Data consistency challenges / distributed transactions

questions.question: How does a HashMap work internally in Java?

rubric.point: Array of buckets indexed by hashCode
Collisions handled by linked list / tree (Java 8+)
equals() used to find the exact key
Resizing when load factor exceeded

questions.question: What is the difference between a list and a tuple in Python? When would you use each?

rubric.point: Lists are mutable, tuples are immutable
Tuples are hashable and can be dict keys
Tuples are slightly faster / lighter

questions.question: Explain how dependency injection works in FastAPI with an example.

rubric.point: Depends() declares dependencies
Used for DB sessions, auth, shared logic
Dependencies can be nested / yield for cleanup
Makes testing easier with dependency overrides

questions.question: How would you handle a 5 GB CSV file with pandas on a machine with 8 GB RAM?

rubric.point: Read in chunks with chunksize
Select only needed columns / dtypes to reduce memory
Use generators / incremental aggregation
Alternatives like Dask, Polars or a database

questions.question: What are Python decorators? Write or describe a decorator that logs execution time.

rubric.point: A decorator is a function that wraps another function
Uses closures / @ syntax
functools.wraps preserves metadata
Measures time with time.time / perf_counter

questions.question: Explain the GIL and how you would speed up CPU-bound vs I/O-bound Python code.

rubric.point: GIL lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time
CPU-bound: multiprocessing or native extensions
I/O-bound: threading or asyncio

questions.question: Write a SQL query to find the second highest salary from an Employees table and explain it.

rubric.point: Uses subquery with MAX or ORDER BY ... LIMIT/OFFSET
Or uses DENSE_RANK window function
Handles duplicates / ties correctly
